h1: The 7 Best Cordless Pruning Saws Under $150 for Trees and Shrubs, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Cordless Pruning Saw Under $150: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 cordless pruning saws under $150 from RYOBI, DeWalt and Greenworks, compared on blade type, battery platform and reach.
summary: The RYOBI HP 18V Brushless 6 inch Pruning Mini Chainsaw Kit is the best cordless pruning saw under $150 for most gardeners, a ready-to-use kit with a brushless motor. The RYOBI 8 inch is the bare-tool pick for existing ONE+ owners, the DeWalt DCCS623B suits the 20V crowd, and the RYOBI one-handed reciprocating saw is the odd, clever option for tight spots.
intro: A pruning saw and a chainsaw are not the same tool, and the difference matters more than any spec. A chain-type pruner is quick through green wood and thick limbs but demands bar oil and respect for kickback. A reciprocating pruning blade is slower, simpler and safer in a tangled shrub. Buying the wrong style is the most common reason a pruning saw ends up on a shelf.

This ranking sorts seven cordless options by blade style, battery platform and kit contents. We reviewed the listings and brand specifications supplied, and we left a generic BLACK+DECKER reciprocating saw out because it is a general demolition tool, not a pruning saw. Where a listing does not say whether a battery is included, we flag it.

products.name: RYOBI HP 18V Brushless 6 in. Compact Pruning Mini Chainsaw Kit
products.verdict: RYOBI's HP brushless 6 inch pruner, sold as a kit and backed by a big battery ecosystem.
products.description:
This RYOBI HP 18V pruner has a brushless motor and a 6 inch bar, sold as a kit at the $100 to $200 level. HP is RYOBI's high-performance line, and it uses the same 18V ONE+ batteries as a very large tool range.

It claims top spot because it combines a brushless motor with kit packaging from a major brand. A brushless motor wastes less battery and runs cooler, which matters on an 18V platform where packs are small. The RYOBI battery family also means spares, chargers and sister tools are easy to find in stores. The 6 inch bar limits you to modest branches, and you should check the listing to confirm what comes in the kit.

Buy it for orchard and garden pruning when you want a dependable brand. Skip it if you need the longest bar.
products.idealFor: Gardeners wanting a dependable branded pruner.

products.name: RYOBI 18V Brushless 8 in. Battery Compact Pruning Mini Chainsaw (Tool Only)
products.verdict: A brushless 8 inch RYOBI pruner for anyone who already owns 18V batteries.
products.description:
The 8 inch RYOBI is a brushless compact pruning chainsaw sold as a tool only, at the $100 to $200 level. You need an 18V RYOBI battery and charger to run it.

It ranks second because the longer bar suits thicker branches than the kit above, and the brushless motor is a proper efficiency win. The bare-tool format makes it very good value for an owner with spare packs, and a poor choice for someone starting out, as the battery is a significant extra cost.

Choose it if you already have RYOBI ONE+ batteries. Skip it if you want everything in one box.
pros: Strong value if you have packs
products.idealFor: RYOBI 18V owners wanting a longer bar.

products.name: Dewalt Chainsaw Pruning CRDLS 20V 8IN DCCS623B
products.verdict: DeWalt's 8 inch 20V pruning saw, built for crews that already use the platform.
products.description:
The DeWalt DCCS623B is a 20V cordless pruning chainsaw with an 8 inch bar, at the $100 to $200 level. DeWalt often uses a B suffix for bare tools, so check whether a battery is included before buying.

It ranks third because it matches the RYOBI 8 inch on bar length but costs more and gives no extra features in the listing. The reasons to pick it are the DeWalt build reputation and the compatibility with a huge 20V battery family used on job sites. If your trucks already run DeWalt packs, it is the natural choice.

Buy it if DeWalt is your battery brand. Skip it if you would be buying a battery just for this saw.
products.skipIf: You would need to buy a pack.

products.name: RYOBI 18V ONE+ One-Handed Pruning Reciprocating Saw Tool Only
products.verdict: A one-handed reciprocating pruning saw for tight shrubs, sold as a bare tool.
products.description:
This RYOBI ONE+ saw is a one-handed reciprocating pruning tool, sold without a battery, at the $50 to $100 level. It uses a straight blade rather than a chain.

It places fourth because a reciprocating blade is slower than a chain but easier to control in a crowded bush. There is no chain oil to manage, no chain tension and less kickback worry, so it suits owners who prune thin to medium wood. The one-handed design lets you hold a branch with the other hand.

Choose it if you value simplicity and own a RYOBI battery. Skip it if you want fast cuts through thick limbs.
pros: No chain oil or tension to manage
products.idealFor: Owners pruning tight shrubs near the house.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 6in Mini Chainsaw, 2.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A complete Greenworks 24V pruner with a 2.0 Ah battery and charger.
products.description:
The Greenworks 24V saw has a 6 inch bar and ships with a 2.0 Ah battery and charger, at the $50 to $100 level.

It ranks fifth because it is a simple, ready-to-run pruner without the brushless motor listing of the RYOBI. For a beginner, the complete kit is the draw: unbox, charge and cut. The 24V battery works across other Greenworks tools, and the brand is easy to find in stores.

Buy it if you want everything in one box at a low price. Skip it if a brushless motor is high on your list.

products.name: ONEAND 18V 6 in. Cordless Battery Compact Pruning MINI Chainsaw Tool ONLY
products.verdict: A low-cost 18V, 6 inch bare tool for people who already own compatible batteries.
products.description:
The ONEAND is an 18V, 6 inch compact pruning mini chainsaw sold as a tool only, at the $50 to $100 level. The listing says little else.

It ranks sixth because the missing detail makes it a gamble: no battery brand fit, no motor type and no oiling information. The ONEAND name is also less familiar than RYOBI or DeWalt. For a person with compatible 18V packs it can be a low-risk experiment, but you need to confirm the battery fit first.

Buy it only after confirming the battery compatibility. Skip it if you want certainty and brand support.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 6 in Mini Pruning Chainsaw, 2.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A twin of the other Greenworks kit, listed in a higher price bucket.
products.description:
This Greenworks 24V mini pruning chainsaw has a 6 inch bar and includes a 2.0 Ah battery and charger, listed at the $100 to $200 level.

It ranks last because it offers the same hardware on paper as the other Greenworks kit but costs more. The cutting capacity is the same, so the only reason to pick this listing is a better current deal.

Buy it only if it is cheaper than the other Greenworks. Skip it otherwise.
products.idealFor: Buyers who find it at a discount.

whatMatters.detail: A chain cuts quickly through thick green wood, but needs oil and careful handling. A reciprocating blade is slower yet simpler and more forgiving in tight shrubs. Choose by the wood you cut most, not by price.

Tool-only listings exclude the battery and charger, which can double the real cost for a newcomer. Kits include both. The words tool only in the title are the giveaway, so read them before checking the price.
Brushless motors run cooler and use less battery than brushed ones, which helps on 18V packs with limited capacity. They add a little cost. Look for brushless in the product name.
A 6 inch bar suits shrubs and thin limbs, while 8 inch handles thicker branches. Longer bars are heavier and harder to hold overhead. Match the bar to your thickest regular cut.
A saw that shares a battery with your other tools saves money. RYOBI ONE+ and DeWalt 20V are the big families here. Check the voltage and the platform name before you buy.

faq.q: Can a pruning saw replace a manual one?
faq.a: For frequent or high-volume work, yes, because a cordless saw saves effort. For occasional cuts, a good manual pruning saw is lighter and has no battery to manage.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with cordless pruning saws?
faq.a: Buying a tool-only model without a compatible battery. The pack and charger can cost as much as the saw, so check what you own before ordering.

faq.q: Is the DeWalt worth it over the RYOBI 8 inch?
faq.a: Only if you own DeWalt batteries. The RYOBI offers the same bar length for less, with a brushless motor named in the listing.
Usually 5 to 10 minutes. Fit the chain and bar, tension it, fill the oil reservoir and charge a battery. A reciprocating saw needs only a blade and a battery.
Wipe off sap after every use, keep the chain oiled and tensioned, and store the battery partly charged. Sap can gum up a blade, so clean it with a little solvent.

faq.q: Can I prune from a ladder?
faq.a: Be cautious. Ladders and chain saws are a risky mix, so use a pole pruner for high branches. A one-handed saw is better kept for work at ground or waist height.

finalTake: The RYOBI HP 18V Brushless 6 inch kit is the best cordless pruning saw under $150, combining a brushless motor with a big battery ecosystem. The RYOBI 8 inch suits ONE+ owners who need more reach, the DeWalt DCCS623B suits the 20V crowd, and the RYOBI reciprocating saw is the safest for tight shrubs. Check what comes in the box before you buy.
